claim: When the parent chain from the start id reaches a repeated id (any parent cycle on the path), path_up returns [] even though the start id names an entry, so the result has no last entry with the start id; D4 rule 1 and path_up's own comment say to stop at the first repeated id and keep the path.
notes: Cause: journal.ail:1405 `else if contains_string(seen, id) then []`, where it should be `then acc`. The eval twin ev_path_up (reader.ail:1226) has `then acc`, and its SOURCE pin (reader.ail:1225, sha256:db222e4c...) matches the current core body only with `then []` changed back to `then acc` (checked with tools/eval_protected/ailspan.py; find_entry, contains_string and fold_journal still match their pins), so the core changed after the twin was pinned and the two now disagree. Execution, real code: every case with a cycle on the path, in every generator: E1 (ids a/b/c, parents ''/a/b/c/absent, every list of length 0-5) 778,095 of 4,068,080; random 28,712 of 100,000 (N<=60) and 7,863 of 20,000 (N<=40); structured (host-shaped chain to 20, one parent redirected) 16,170 of 30,105; linear chains of 250-2,000 entries with root.parent=leaf. ev_path_up has no violation on any of them. Negative control: r1 exits 0 on a control copy with only `then acc` restored. P5.1 and P5.2 still hold, trivially, since [] has no repeats. Reachability: the host writer (session-journal.ts append) sets parent_id to the previous leaf and fresh zero-padded ids, so it does not write cycles; a cycle needs a hand-edited, corrupt or foreign journal, or the future branch/rewind operations D8 announces. Effect on the fold: A2-T5-2.

claim: The real, unmodified fold_journal refuses with Refusal::Header, whose message says 'the first entry on the path is not a header', when the header's parent_id points back at an entry on the leaf's chain. D4 rule 1's path there is the whole chain with the header first, and the eval twin eval_fold_journal folds the same journal to the unmodified journal's state.
witness: 7-entry journal from journal_lines_of_records (0000 header ... 0006 leaf, history 3 messages), header 0000's parent_id set to "0006" (or "0003" or "0000"), folded at leaf 0006: fold_journal = Err(header); eval_fold_journal = Ok(history 3), the same as the unmodified journal
notes: X-2 (metamorphic, from D4 rule 1): pointing the header's parent_id at an id already on the leaf's path does not change rule 1's path, so the fold must not change. Root cause: A2-T5-1 (path_up returns [], and fold_journal maps an empty path to Err(Header), journal.ail:1685-1686). fold_diff.ail runs all 441 single-parent_id redirections of the journal (each entry x each id, '' or an absent id x each leaf). Exactly 28 differ between fold_journal and eval_fold_journal: the header-closing cycles with the leaf at or below the redirect target. The other 413 agree, including cycles that close below the header, where both refuse with header. Negative control: r2 exits 0 when the same harness folds with the control core (`then acc`). Reachability: as A2-T5-1, from --resume over a journal containing such a cycle.

claim: When an entry's id is the empty string and the start id is "", path_up returns [] because its first test (`if id == "" then acc`) treats "" as the root marker before looking the id up, so a start id that names an entry gives no entry with that id.
witness: es=[{id:"",parent_id:""}], path_up(es,"",[],[]) = [] (find_entry(es,"") = Some(entry 0)); also es=[x<-'', ''<-x] from "" = []; the reader's exported strict_path accepts both lists from "" and returns [entry 0] and [x, ''] respectively
notes: E2 (ids ''/a/b, parents ''/a/b/absent, every list of length 0-4): 17,940 of 90,484 cases, every case where the start is "" and some entry has id "". A second real function disagrees with path_up here: the eval reader's exported strict_path (reader.ail:1713) looks up a "" leaf and accepted 6,485 of these cases with a non-empty path, while path_up returned []. Wherever strict_path accepts a non-empty-id start (34,866 E1 cases, 4,350 random, 8,855 structured), it agrees with path_up exactly. The eval twin does the same (journal.ail:1404 and reader.ail:1227), so this predates the twin's pin and is a design gap, not the planted change. Reachability is low: journal_entry_of_json (journal.ail:712) accepts "id": "" with no non-empty check, and journal_leaf returns "" when the last line's id is "", in which case the fold refuses with Header instead of reporting a malformed id; the host's entryId pads seq, so the host never writes "". Negative control: r3 exits 0 on a control copy whose path_up looks the id up before treating "" as the root; it still exits 1 with only the A2-T5-1 fix applied.

claim: path_up's running time grows quadratically with the path length on host-shaped linear journals: t(4N)/t(N) was 15-19 for N=200 against 4-6 for a linear-scan control, about 1.3 s for a 400-entry path and 5 s for 800, so every resume pays O(entries^2) before folding.
witness: a linear chain of N entries in the host's order (entry k's parent is entry k-1, root first, leaf last), path_up from the leaf; N=200 against N=800
notes: Efficiency, exploratory. Each step calls find_entry, which rescans es from the head (N x L), and contains_string, which scans seen (L^2); in the host's journals L = N. The same file avoids `++ [m]` because a quadratic cost is wrong 'in the thing the journal exists to make cheap' (journal.ail:1431), and that reasoning applies here too. Recursion depth is not the problem: path_up, find_entry and contains_string all run under --max-recursion-depth 50 on a 500-entry path, and find_entry scans 1,000,000 entries. Measured in-process with std/clock on a shared machine (other sessions' ailang processes were running), so the threshold is a ratio of 10, set between the measured linear control (3.9-6.0) and path_up (15.3-18.9). The real journals in the tree (.agent/.../plan003-p4-live-gate) have 10-23 entries; the cost only shows on long sessions.
